title: Habitat reference: every physical assumption of the two-module habitat, in one reviewable file

reviewers: University of Houston, aerospace (life support): the ventilation and filter model, the scrubber constants, the crew rates
review.howToReplay: edit a value, keep the file, run `npm run habitat:build` then `npm test`; the document's manifest records the sha256 of this file, so a result always names the assumptions it was computed with

units.time: seconds of session (the story speaks in minutes; the build script converts)
units.co2: ppm (mole fraction times a million) in the volumes; kg/s between nodes
units.flow: m3/s between nodes; the station documents m3/min

model.reference: plugins/habitat (this repository) on the substrate's Physics.Scene:atmosphere; the equations are in each node's card, plugins/habitat/docs
model.states: the CO2 mass of each volume (the atmosphere, ideal gas), the scrubber's flow (a lag), the fan's speed (a spin-up), the filter's loading
equations: atmosphere   dm_CO2/dt = sum of the delta_CO2_k inputs                                  [kg/s]; ppm = n_CO2 / n_total * 1e6
scrubber     d(flow)/dt = (flowAtFull * command - flow) / lag; removal = efficiency * flow * co2MassPerM3(ppm)   [kg/s]
fan          Q = s * sqrt(k / (R + k / Qfree^2)), k = capacityFactor * shutoffPressure, R = ductResistance + filter.resistance; d(s)/dt = (command - s) / spinUp
filter       resistance = clean * (1 + loading / loadingDoubling); d(loading)/dt = captureEfficiency * dust * Q
duct, hatch  flux = Q * (co2MassPerM3(ppmA) - co2MassPerM3(ppmB)); deltaA = -flux, deltaB = +flux
whatIsNotModelled: the exchange of species other than CO2 (a thousandth of the air, no pressure effect)
an efficiency of the scrubber that depends on the inlet concentration (NASA's ground tests show it; library nasa-scrubber-test-protocols)
the fan driven by a motor node (its speed ratio is the command through a spin-up; a motor will set it later)
dust settling under gravity (the scene carries the gravity; the substrate's particulate node is a V1 stub)

preset.source: the substrate's lunar preset: 1.625 m/s2, the scene the cabin twin already uses

volumeM3.source: as built; the design drawing gives 32 with the racks not yet installed
volumeM3.status: the truth the commissioning measures; a twin never reads it

initialCo2Ppm.source: the sensor co2-1 at the start of the test

volumeM3.source: as built, the living quarters and the rest of the pressurised volume
volumeM3.status: the truth; a twin never reads it

initialCo2Ppm.source: the sensor co2-2 at the start of the test

activity.source: two operators at work in the Lab
the two others at rest in Hab-B

sleep.source: NASA BVAD Rev2 Table 3-26, reference crewmember asleep (band 0.17 to 0.28)

rest.source: NASA BVAD Rev2, between asleep and awake; library nasa-crew-metabolic-loads

light_work.source: inside NASA's awake band (0.26 to 0.45, reference 0.38): people at work sit above the reference
light_work.status: the truth of this crew; a twin knows the band, never this number

heavy_work.source: NASA HIDH 2014: exercise at 75 % VO2max gives about 2.7; heavy work well below

co2DensityKgPerM3.source: ideal gas, CO2 at 101325 Pa and 295.15 K

flowAtFullM3ps.source: library scrubber-1-datasheet: 3.3 m3/min at full command, anemometer at the outlet

efficiency.source: datasheet: 0.30 single-pass; 0.30303 makes the effective flow exactly 1.0 m3/min (the datasheet rounds)

lagTimeConstantMinutes.source: datasheet: first order, step of the command

habitatScale.source: the bench's motor scaled to the habitat's machine; the cabin twin's assumption

designFlowM3ps.source: the station's design: 3 m3/min between the Lab and Hab-B with the hatch closed, a clean filter and the fan at full command
designFlowM3ps.status: designed; what is delivered is measured

shutoffPressurePa.source: a small axial duct fan's curve, left end

freeDeliveryM3ps.source: the same curve, right end (5.4 m3/min)

ductResistance.source: the duct without the filter: 50 Pa at the design flow

fanEfficiency.source: air power over electrical power, a small axial fan

cleanResistance.source: chosen so that the clean system delivers the design flow: 250 / 0.05^2 - 250 / 0.09^2 - 20000; 123 Pa across the clean filter at the design flow

loadingDoublingKg.source: 50 g of dust doubles the resistance, a pleated filter's order

captureEfficiency.source: a fine filter on habitat dust

ambientDustKgPerM3.source: 1 mg/m3, a third of NASA's 3 mg/m3 total dust limit (library nasa-co2-limits)

endOfLifeLoadingKg.source: four doublings: 16 times the clean resistance

initialLoadingKg.source: the fault of this commissioning: a filter already fouled, so the fan delivers 2.0 m3/min where the design says 3
initialLoadingKg.status: the truth the commissioning measures; a twin never reads it

openExchangeM3ps.source: an inter-module ventilation's order with the hatch open, 140 cfm on the ISS (library nasa-scrubber-test-protocols)

closedLeakM3ps.source: nothing documented for the seals; the ventilation, not the seals, is how the modules exchange

solverStepSeconds.source: one sample per six seconds resolves minutes-long dynamics; ten per story minute
